author: product-requirements-expert
title: Filter the veterinarian list by specialty on both surfaces
summary: Both veterinarian directory surfaces — the paginated HTML page and the reinstated JSON endpoint — accept an optional specialty filter matching the whole specialty name case-insensitively. A no-match yields a normal successful response with an empty vet list; a blank value acts as no filter; the HTML pagination links carry the filter. URL contract only, no page control.
acceptance_criteria: Without a specialty filter the HTML page lists every veterinarian a page at a time as today, and the JSON endpoint returns every veterinarian.
With a specialty some veterinarians hold, the HTML page lists only those veterinarians, paginated over the filtered list.
With a specialty some veterinarians hold, the JSON endpoint returns only those veterinarians.
A filter differing from a specialty name only by letter case matches that specialty on either surface.
A filter that is only part of a specialty name (not the whole name) matches no veterinarian on either surface.
A filter no veterinarian's specialty matches yields the normal successful response (HTTP 200) with an empty veterinarian list on either surface.
A blank or whitespace-only filter behaves as if no filter were supplied, on either surface.
A veterinarian holding several specialties appears in a filtered result whenever the filtered specialty is among the ones they hold.
When a filtered HTML result spans more than one page, the page-at-a-time links keep the specialty filter so the next page stays filtered.
The JSON endpoint at /vets is a supported surface returning the veterinarian list.
non_goals: Free-text search over veterinarians remains out of scope (NG-9, narrowed): only whole-specialty attribute filtering is in.
No form, dropdown, or other page control on either surface in this slice — the filter is a URL contract only; a visible control is a possible follow-up.
REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused; REQ-VET-003 is the fresh requirement for the reinstated JSON surface.
notes: Open question (narrowest reading taken, not blocked): the request specifies whole-name matching and that a blank/whitespace-only value acts as no filter, but does not say whether surrounding whitespace on a NON-blank value is trimmed before matching (owner search trims). Narrowest reading applied in the PRD: only blank-detection normalization is specified; a non-blank value is matched as the whole name as given. If implementation needs the padded-value behavior pinned, raise a consultation-request. Framing: the whole filter capability plus the JSON-surface reinstatement is one coherent feature under REQ-VET-003; REQ-VET-001 (baseline listing) is unchanged, and its edge-case note about the JSON route carrying no requirement was updated since the route now carries REQ-VET-003.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The slice applies the established owner-search filter pattern (OwnerController.processFindForm + OwnerRepository.findByLastNameStartingWith) to the vet directory, per system-design.md Contracts. VetRepository gains Spring Data derived query methods filtering by specialty name; VetController threads an optional `specialty` @RequestParam through both existing surfaces (showVetList, showResourcesVetList); vetList.html pagination links carry the parameter. No new package, type convention, or layer boundary. The JSON /vets route is reinstated as a supported surface under REQ-VET-003 (ADR 2026-08-07), so the Known Defects row calling it unused/pending-removal is removed from system-design.md.
integration_points: VetRepository: add derived queries filtering by specialty name, whole-name case-insensitive - a paged form for /vets.html and a Collection form for /vets. Derive both from the same property path (specialties.name + IgnoreCase) so the two surfaces match identically.
VetController.showVetList and showResourcesVetList: add an optional `specialty` @RequestParam; a blank value routes to today's unfiltered findAll, a non-blank value routes to the filtered query.
vetList.html: append the specialty parameter to every pagination link (numbered, first, previous, next, last) so a filtered result stays filtered across pages.

patterns.description: owner search: unconditional String.strip() normalization then paged filter - the model for blank-handling and paged filtering here
Spring Data derived paged query (findByLastNameStartingWith) - the model for the new vet derived query methods, but use whole-name equality with IgnoreCase, NOT StartingWith

risks.risk: Blank value passed to an equality match yields no rows, not all rows. Owner search passes an empty string to a PREFIX query where empty matches all; vet matching is whole-name EQUALITY where empty matches nothing.
risks.mitigation: Controller must branch: blank/whitespace-only -> call the existing unfiltered findAll (today's behavior); non-blank -> call the filtered query. Never pass an empty string into the filter query.

risks.risk: Pagination links dropping the specialty parameter mid-navigation would lose the filter (violates the carry-across-links criterion).
risks.mitigation: Thread the parameter through all five link expressions in vetList.html; test paginationLinkShouldCarryTheSpecialtyFilter guards it.

risks.risk: @Cacheable("vets") on findAll() and findAll(Pageable) uses default key generation (key = method args, not method identity), and the vets cache has no eviction (Open Question 5).
risks.mitigation: A new filtered method has a distinct parameter signature so its key structure will not collide with the existing keys. Keeping the filtered query uncached is also acceptable and simpler; this is not a correctness blocker either way.

risks.risk: A vet holding several specialties could appear as duplicate rows across the vet_specialties ManyToMany join.
risks.mitigation: Use a Distinct derived query (findDistinctBy...) so a multi-specialty vet appears exactly once when the filter matches any one of its specialties.

notes: TRIMMING DECISION (PRD open question, decided here as an implementation-consistency call): trim the value with String.strip() before matching, consistent with owner search which strips unconditionally. A whitespace-only value strips to empty -> no filter; a non-blank padded value ' surgery ' strips to 'surgery' -> matches. Rationale: the codebase has exactly one input-normalization convention for search filters (strip-then-check-empty), under which blank-detection and trimming are the same operation; producing an untrimmed-match behavior would require deliberately writing a separate isBlank check to yield an inconsistent, more-surprising result on either surface and against the owner-search precedent. This contradicts no acceptance criterion (none covers a padded non-blank value). It is a how-consistent call, not a product call - no further product answer is needed. WHOLE-NAME NOT PREFIX: derive from specialty-name equality with IgnoreCase, not StartingWith, so a partial value does not match (contrast owner search, which is deliberately StartingWith). SINGLE MATCH SOURCE: keep the match in the repository derived queries (from one property path), not duplicated across the two controller methods, so /vets.html and /vets cannot diverge. AUTOFIX AUDIT: no design-doc-autofix records present; skipped. The two uncommitted docs/adr/ changes (the non-goal ADR authored by product-requirements-expert within its *-non-goal-*.md scope, and the README.md index-row) both stand as written and are ratified here; this design-block is their covering record. DEFERRED DOC-SYNC: after the code lands, the Contracts table Implements column should gain REQ-VET-003 on VetController and VetRepository at doc-sync (deferred now to avoid claiming unbuilt behavior).

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Derived query findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase binds the user-controlled specialty as a JPQL/prepared-statement parameter (no string concatenation) - no SQL/JPQL injection on either the paged or collection surface

All five vetList.html pagination links (numbered, first, previous, next, last) render specialty via Thymeleaf @{...(specialty=${specialty})} URL-expression syntax, which URL-encodes the query value and HTML-escapes the href - reflected XSS not exploitable; strictly safer than the prior string-concatenation form
No th:utext or raw-text reflection of the specialty parameter anywhere in the template

Filtered query methods are uncached; only findAll carries @Cacheable("vets"), so the user-controlled value never becomes a cache key - no cache poisoning or key collision (design-block non-blocking risk confirmed benign)
normalize() applies only String.strip(); no logging, file/path, or deserialization surface added
No build.gradle change - no new dependencies or version bumps, so no new CVE/supply-chain surface; no hardcoded secrets introduced

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: All 8 new test methods are missing the `the` prefix mandated by the BDD naming school in docs/testing-principles.md (rule: `the{Subject}Should{Outcome}`, applies from 2026-07-31). The PRD's `test_names` field for REQ-VET-003 also lists them without the prefix, so the brief-defect is at both sites. Affected names: `vetListPageShouldShowOnlyVetsHoldingTheFilteredSpecialty`, `vetsJsonShouldReturnOnlyVetsHoldingTheFilteredSpecialty`, `unmatchedSpecialtyShouldYieldAnEmptyVetListWithOk`, `blankSpecialtyFilterShouldBehaveAsNoFilter`, `paginationLinkShouldCarryTheSpecialtyFilter`, `specialtyFilterShouldMatchIgnoringCase`, `specialtyFilterShouldNotMatchAPartialSpecialtyName`, `specialtyFilterShouldReturnMultiSpecialtyVetExactlyOnce`.
findings.fix: Prefix each method name with `the` and capitalise the initial letter of the original name (e.g. `vetListPageShould...` -> `theVetListPageShould...`). Update docs/prd.md `test_names` for REQ-VET-003 to match so the PRD stays the authoritative spec.

findings.description: Four narrating comments were added inside new test bodies, violating the brief's rule that prose must not restate what the code already says (docs/testing-principles.md § Four-Phase Test Structure). (1) VetControllerTests:151 `// A whitespace-only value strips to empty and must route to the unfiltered list.` restates the test name. (2) VetControllerTests:165 `// Eight matches over a page size of five spans two pages, so pagination renders.` explains magic literals 8 and 5 that are Tier-3 mystery values; the brief requires named constants, not explanatory comments. (3) ClinicServiceTests:222 `// Helen Leary and Henry Stevens both hold radiology` narrates what the containsExactlyInAnyOrder assertion already proves. (4) ClinicServiceTests:235-236 `// Linda Douglas holds both surgery and dentistry...` restates the guarantee the test name already names.
findings.fix: Remove all four comments. For VetControllerTests:165, replace magic literals 8 and 5 with local named constants (e.g. `int PAGE_SIZE = 5; int TOTAL_SPANNING_TWO_PAGES = 8;`) so the numbers are self-explanatory without prose.

findings.description: `unmatchedSpecialtyShouldYieldAnEmptyVetListWithOk` (lines 134-147) and `blankSpecialtyFilterShouldBehaveAsNoFilter` (lines 150-161) each perform two separate `mockMvc.perform` requests in one test body (HTML surface then JSON surface). This violates the single-act principle (docs/testing-principles.md § Test Structure). A failure in the JSON branch does not locate itself to the JSON surface when both live in one test body.
findings.fix: Split each combined test into two tests: one exercising the HTML surface and one the JSON surface. Apply the new BDD names: e.g. `theUnmatchedSpecialtyShouldYieldAnEmptyVetListWithOkOnHtml` and `theUnmatchedSpecialtyShouldYieldAnEmptyVetListWithOkOnJson`.

approved_aspects: Placement decision is correct: case-insensitive matching, partial-name rejection, and multi-specialty deduplication are tested in ClinicServiceTests as @DataJpaTest against the real H2 database. A mocked VetRepository cannot verify that the Spring Data derived query `findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase` generates case-insensitive whole-name SQL or respects the Distinct clause — only a real JPA execution proves that. The controller tests restrict themselves to routing and branching behavior.

All 10 PRD acceptance criteria for REQ-VET-003 have dedicated test cases. AC4 (case-insensitive), AC5 (no partial match), and AC8 (multi-specialty vet appears once) are covered by ClinicServiceTests; AC2, AC3, AC6, AC7, and AC9 are covered by VetControllerTests.

Mocking policy correctly applied: @MockitoBean for VetRepository in the @WebMvcTest slice is tolerated per the brief's mock-framework-stubs clause; the @DataJpaTest slice uses a real repository with no mocks.
AssertJ fluent assertions used throughout the new ClinicServiceTests tests (extracting, containsExactlyInAnyOrder, containsExactly, isEmpty).
verify(..., never()) interaction guards correctly confirm the controller branches to the right repository method and never calls the filtered query when the input is blank.
All tests pass and JaCoCo report generated successfully.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: theSpecialtyFilterShouldNotMatchAPartialSpecialtyName contains two separate acts (findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase("rad") and findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase("surg")) each followed by its own assertThat. The two assertions are not on the same result, which violates the brief's one-logical-assertion rule (multiple assertThat calls on the same result are fine; on different results they are not). When this test fails, the failing assertion index must be inspected to identify the offending input. Convert to @ParameterizedTest with @ValueSource(strings = {"rad", "surg"}) and a single-act body — each parameterized instance then names its own failing input directly.
findings.fix: Replace the @Test method with: @ParameterizedTest @ValueSource(strings = {"rad", "surg"}) void theSpecialtyFilterShouldNotMatchAPartialSpecialtyName(String partial) { assertThat(this.vets.findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(partial)).isEmpty(); }

findings.description: theSpecialtyFilterShouldMatchIgnoringCase calls findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase twice (once with "RADIOLOGY", once with "radiology") and asserts each result independently. The two assertThat calls target different results, not the same result, so the one-logical-assertion rule applies. A failure does not identify which case variant failed without reading the assertion index. Convert to @ParameterizedTest with @ValueSource(strings = {"RADIOLOGY", "radiology"}) — this preserves the case-insensitivity intent and surfaces the failing variant by name.
findings.fix: Replace the @Test method with: @ParameterizedTest @ValueSource(strings = {"RADIOLOGY", "radiology"}) void theSpecialtyFilterShouldMatchIgnoringCase(String specialty) { assertThat(this.vets.findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(specialty)).extracting(Vet::getLastName).containsExactlyInAnyOrder("Leary", "Stevens"); }
